newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian police arrest suspected mafia killer.
newsitem.headline: Belgian police arrest suspected mafia killer.

text.p: Police in Liege on Wednesday arrested a Sicilian man, suspected of being a mafia killer on charges of having murdered two other members of a mafia family, Belga news agency said.
It said Angelo Romano, 41, was being held in the city's Lantin prison on an international arrest warrant issued in Palermo, awaiting extradition to Sicily.

Liege, scene of the mafia-style contract killing in July 1991 of Socialist Party patriarch Andre Cools, is known as the Palermo of Belgium because of its extensive Italian connections and links with orgnised crime.
Six people, including former government minister Alain Van der Biest and his one-time private secretary Richard Taxquet, have been arrested in the past month for the killing of Cools.

An international arrest warrant has been issued for the two alleged Sicilian-based Tunisian assassins who are said by lawyers for some of the arrested men to have been paid 750,000 francs ($25,000) for the killing.
